queries.q: CUDA driver API thread safety: can multiple host threads call driver API functions concurrently
queries.excerpt: A host thread may have only one device context current at a time. When a context is created with `cuCtxCreate()`, it is made current to the calling host thread. CUDA functions that operate in a context (most functions that do not involve device enumeration or context management) will return `CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_CONTEXT` if a valid context is not current to the thread.
queries.claim: (1) A libcuda.so segfault can be triggered by concurrent use of CUDA contexts/streams from several host threads in one process

queries.q: multiple CUDA contexts per device in one process from several host threads, context switching cost and primary context
queries.excerpt: A CUDA context is analogous to a CPU process. All resources and actions performed within the driver API are encapsulated inside a CUDA context, and the system automatically cleans up these resources when the context is destroyed. Besides objects such as modules and texture or surface references, each context has its own distinct address space.
queries.claim: (1) multiple contexts per device per process: each context has its own address space; docs describe the model and say nothing about crashes or a thread-safety guarantee

queries.q: all CUDA driver API functions are thread-safe; multiple threads may call the driver API simultaneously
driver crash or segmentation fault when running CUDA tests concurrently in parallel threads in the same process
